restatements.text: Prohibits county jails from keeping individuals in custody past their regular release time solely because of a federal immigration detainer.

evidence.quote: No county jail may hold a person beyond the time the person would otherwise be released solely on the basis of a detainer request from federal immigration authorities.
evidence.why: It restricts the detention powers of county jails by forbidding them from holding individuals beyond their normal release times based on federal detainers.

evidence.quote: No county jail may hold a person beyond the time the person would otherwise be released solely on the basis of a detainer request from federal immigration authorities.
evidence.why: It expands legal protections for immigrants by banning jails from holding them past their scheduled release times for federal immigration purposes.

evidence.quote: No county jail may hold a person beyond the time the person would otherwise be released solely on the basis of a detainer request from federal immigration authorities.
evidence.why: It imposes a statewide prohibition, overriding the ability of individual counties to set their own policies on immigration detainers.

evidence.quote: No county jail may hold a person beyond the time the person would otherwise be released solely on the basis of a detainer request from federal immigration authorities.
evidence.why: It prohibits local jails from cooperating with federal immigration authorities by extending a person's detention.

evidence.quote: No county jail may hold a person beyond the time the person would otherwise be released solely on the basis of a detainer request from federal immigration authorities.
evidence.why: It strengthens fair procedures by ensuring individuals are not subjected to prolonged confinement based solely on a federal detainer once their underlying reason for detention ends.

evidence.quote: No county jail may hold a person beyond the time the person would otherwise be released solely on the basis of a detainer request from federal immigration authorities.
evidence.why: It removes local governments' authority to decide whether their jails will honor federal immigration detainers.

analysis.answer: Currently, each county decides whether its jail will honor federal immigration detainer requests. This measure establishes a uniform statewide rule prohibiting county jails from holding individuals past their standard release time solely due to a federal immigration detainer.

Jails will release individuals at their scheduled times rather than holding them for federal agents. In response, federal immigration authorities may have to conduct apprehensions in the community or take custody before the scheduled release time.

It addresses the issue of prolonged detention of immigrants and varying county policies on federal detainer cooperation. By banning local jail holds, it removes a tool used by federal authorities, potentially creating an incentive for federal agents to conduct broader community enforcement operations if they cannot apprehend individuals at the jail.

The state government gains authority by setting a uniform rule that preempts local discretion. Immigrants subject to detainers gain protection from extended detention. County sheriffs and local officials lose the discretion to honor these requests.

The public safety impact of local non-cooperation with immigration enforcement is disputed. Some researchers find that such policies do not increase local crime rates and may improve community cooperation with local police, while others contend that releasing deportable individuals increases the risk of subsequent offenses in the community.
